findings.title: Session closed twice: Cleanup plus explicit Close
findings.message: The new `t.Cleanup(s.Close)` registers a close, but the loop body still calls `s.Close()` explicitly. On the success path each session is closed twice. If `Close` is not idempotent (for example, it closes a channel or stops a goroutine), the cleanup will panic or hang after the test passes.
findings.suggestion: Close each session only once. Either remove the explicit `s.Close()` at the end of the loop body and rely on the cleanup, or make sure `Close` is idempotent (for example, guard it with `sync.Once`).

fix.before:
s := New()
		t.Cleanup(s.Close)
		call(t, s, "example.load", ExampleLoadParams{ID: id}, "load")
		call(t, s, "simulation.pause", struct{}{}, "pause")
		snap := settled(t, s)
		if snap.Mixed == nil || len(snap.Mixed.Thermal) == 0 {
			t.Fatal("thermal example", id, snap.Diagnostics)
		}
		call(t, s, "simulation.step", StepParams{Duration: .0001}, "step")
		s.Close()
	}

findings.title: Editing thermal parameters silently enables thermal modeling
findings.message: The thermal parameter and self-heating handlers in `desktop/thermal_controls.go` are recorded here as calling `apply(next, true)`. They always send `Enabled: true`, so editing a coefficient or toggling self-heating on a part with thermal modeling disabled turns the model on as a side effect. The user did not ask for that.
findings.suggestion: In `desktop/thermal_controls.go`, pass the current `enabled` state to `apply` instead of the hard-coded `true`, i.e. `apply(next, enabled)`. Alternatively, disable these inputs while thermal modeling is off. The inventory entries here are generated, so regenerate them after changing the source.

findings.title: Redundant x-model-id assignment overwritten later
findings.message: In the `thermal.configure` case, the `x-model-id` assignment inside the switch is dead code. Later, `schema["x-model-id"] = ExtendedModelID` runs unconditionally and replaces it. The value is then set again by the new `if id == "thermal.configure"` block. Having two assignments makes it unclear which one controls the result.
findings.suggestion: Remove the assignment inside the switch case. Keep only the post-switch override, which matches how the jfet and current-device cases are handled.

finding.title: Unicode minus in machine-facing temperature description
finding.message: The schema description uses U+2212 MINUS SIGN in "−40". Agents or clients that copy this example will send text the float parser rejects, because the parser expects an ASCII '-'. The text also does not say whether a °C suffix is accepted.
finding.suggestion: Use an ASCII hyphen-minus (-40..125) in the published description, and state explicitly whether a unit suffix is allowed.
